Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
635 AM EDT Thu Aug 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 138 AM EDT Thursday...

A period of humid conditions with showers and thunderstorms remains 
on track.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 138 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Bermuda high pattern will set up today through next Tuesday, 
which will bring warm, humid conditions and chances for showers and 
thunderstorms. A few will be capable of locally heavy rain.

2. Following a seasonably warm and humid period, drier air will 
arrive by the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 138 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Analysis shows strong Bermuda high slowly backing to the 
east as an upper trough is carving itself out. This upper trough 
will deepen into an upper low, and this will set the stage for muggy 
conditions with hit-or-miss shower and thunderstorm activity. Warm, 
moist advection is already producing some showers around Lake 
Ontario as moisture rounds a 500mb ridge axis along coastal New 
England. Increasingly humid conditions will push dewpoints towards 
70 as the day wears on. An incoming trough will provide a focus for 
showers and storms mid-morning through this evening. With no capping 
in place, activity will likely get underway across northern New 
York, maybe even by the time this is published, but most likely mid 
to late this morning. Temperatures will climb into the 80s by 
afternoon, and this will generate plenty of surface-based 
instability, especially across northern New York. The benefit to 
having no capping is that early convection will produce plenty of 
clouds that will extend northeast in 50-60 knot flow in the upper 
levels, which will limit solar heating and could prevent heat 
indices from creeping into the mid 90s. Still with heat indices in 
the mid 80s to lower 90s, it will feel a bit uncomfortable, today. 
So seek shade and drink plenty of water if doing prolonged 
activities. 

This warmth and humidity will help bring PWATs to near 2". Combined 
with 1000-1500 J/kg of CAPE and trough providing some focus, some 
heavy downpours will be likely. A few thunderstorms may be strong. 0-
6km bulk shear values are at the bottom threshold for marginal 
organization (~25 kts), and the newer RRFS suggests some clustering 
is possible. Sounding profiles match schematics for wet microbursts, 
and so any stronger thunderstorm may produce gusty winds. However, 
this will be conditional upon whether mid-morning to early afternoon 
convection may limit instability through increased cloud cover.

Precipitation chances will dwindle tonight, but not completely hit 
zero with very moist conditions in place. Dewpoints remain high 
behind the trough, and so nighttime lows in the mid 60s to lower 70s 
is expected. Friday's conditions will be similar with 80s across the 
region. For tomorrow, there won't be quite as much precipitation due 
to a lack of a trough, and so we may have a better shot at 
approaching mid 90s heat indices, but will give things time to see 
how dewpoints trend over the course of today. By Friday evening 
through Saturday night, a messy conglomerate of troughs will angle 
northeast. Even with the loss of daytime heating, some showers and a 
few rumbles could still take place during the overnight hours. Each 
day should get a little bit cooler at the very least.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The start of next week will feature seasonably 
warm conditions, although less humid compared to previous days 
as the Bermuda high weakens and westerly flows prevails across 
the region. Highs at the start of the week will be in the upper 
70s to mid 80s, but by the middle of the week they will drop a 
few degrees to be in the lower 70s and low 80s. A cold front 
looks to move through the region sometime late Monday into 
Tuesday, bringing widespread showers and a few possible 
thunderstorms, although the timing of the boundary will have a 
large influence on any convective elements. Towards the middle 
of next week, guidance suggests that drier conditions return, 
although we'll have to see as we get closer. 

.KEY MESSAGE 3... 
Bullet: 

Discussion

&&

.AVIATION /12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 12Z Friday...VFR conditions currently prevail at all
terminals and will continue through much of the morning, with
some clouds continuing to stream into the region.  Showers and 
a few thunderstorms are expected to develop throughout the 
afternoon and early evening hours, most likely between 18Z to 
00Z, with the potential for reduced flight conditions within any
of these showers. The better chances for reduced flight 
conditions will be across northern New York, especially KSLK, 
where greater chances for shower activity is expected. Given the
uncertainty in the areal extent and timing of any showers,
PROB30 groups were used to highlight the most likely time
frames. Light southerly flow is expected across the region 
tomorrow, with some locally higher gusts possible within any 
thunderstorm activity. Some guidance supports fog development 
at the very end of the forecast period, especially at any 
terminals that receive showers, but there is still a lot of 
uncertainty so have mostly just hinted at that potential.

Sunday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Monday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
